contents.text: The properties of phospholipids determine their orientation within the lipid bilayer. The heads are polar and hydrophilic, so each head touches either the fluid in the outside environment or the cytoplasm inside the cell. The tails are nonpolar and hydrophobic, so they form the inner core of the membrane, away from fluid.

contents.text: This arrangement prevents certain molecules from crossing the lipid bilayer on their own. The phospholipids are tightly packed, which means large molecules cannot fit between them. Small nonpolar molecules can cross, but ions and most polar molecules cannot cross because they are repelled by the nonpolar fatty acid tails. Some very small polar molecules, like water, are able to pass through, but they do so at a slow rate.
